library.scope: Unchanged pinned standard-library modules, copied by the existing frozen-library generator; not a rewritten posixpath implementation.

errnoDiagnosis.observedSource: The native VM exposes an empty ERROR_CODES table on targets outside Unix, Windows and WASI, including wasm32-unknown-unknown. The Boxes bridge already uses Linux values; its supported catalog now owns numbers/text for fault mapping, errno and strerror.

change: Register os.path and sys.modules[os.path] as the same pinned posixpath module during the existing filesystem bootstrap.
Native fsencode/fsdecode use RustPython UTF-8/surrogateescape codecs, preserve byte/string inputs and consume the native path-like protocol. Keyword filename is supported.

One supported Linux errno catalog supplies constants, errorcode reverse lookup, strerror and native fault numbers/subclasses. Authorization aliases preserve the original source code while using EACCES numerically; unknown codes retain their name/message and no invented errno.
Filesystem-aware library operations use the existing native stat/lstat/readlink/fstat/cwd and authorized R2 actions; lexical operations stay in the guest.
coverage: Module identity through os.path, import os.path, posixpath and restored sys.modules; saved native-heap functions survive closed Worker replacement.
Lexical str/bytes joins, normalization, common/relative paths, file extension, mixed-type rejection and path-like input.
UTF-8 conversions, NUL and non-UTF-8 surrogateescape roundtrip without expanding the UTF-8 filesystem path contract.
Environment-backed expanduser/expandvars, including bytes; updated environment after context reentry.
Metadata predicates, dangling exists versus lexists, size, samefile and sameopenfile against actual sandbox bytes.
Strict str/bytes realpath, missing targets, symlink cycles with ELOOP and non-directory traversal with ENOTDIR.
Read-only restored context reads canonical bytes but cannot create files. Execute-only context observes no metadata and strict realpath raises PermissionError.
Native fault classification for EAGAIN/EINTR/EPIPE and permission aliases; unknown source errors preserved.
